title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Directors, Managing Director, Company Secretary, Executive Management Team, and any other employee (full-time, part-time or casual); plus anyone who by role or otherwise becomes aware of Inside Information via access to confidential material; plus any other person the Company designates as aware of or working on a market-sensitive matter.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Employees who are Directors; distinguished for approval (Chair, or Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair's own dealings) and for Disposal Consent during Black-out Periods.

tiers.name: Consultants or contractors
tiers.description: Consultants or contractors who are not Employees; subject only to the Inside Information prohibition, not to Black-out Periods, the approval process or the notification/margin loan restrictions that apply to Employees.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Deemed 'Employees': spouse or children (including step-children) under 18; a trust of which the person, family members or a family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary; and a company the person or their family controls.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

windows.start_anchor: 15 trading days prior to release of the Company's quarterly report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: 15 trading days prior to release of the Company's half-year financial report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's half-year financial report

windows.start_anchor: 15 trading days prior to release of the Company's annual financial report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's annual financial report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Chair and/or Managing Director, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may determine any other period to be a Black-out Period from time to time. Confidentiality of such periods is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using Derivatives (expressly defined to include options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars, plus any risk-limiting product) in relation to unvested equity instruments including performance rights.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Same absolute ban extends to vested Company Securities subject to a disposal restriction such as a Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Derivatives may be used over vested, unrestricted positions subject to the law and the rest of the Policy, i.e. prior written approval (Executive Director/CEO, or Chair for Directors), outside Black-out Periods, and only absent Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Hedging is not a separately named concept; it is folded into the definition of Derivatives as 'any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities', which is banned outright for unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: The same risk-limiting-product definition of Derivatives is banned outright for vested Company Securities subject to a disposal restriction.
rules.evidence: vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock')

rules.detail: A risk-limiting transaction over vested, unrestricted shares is permitted subject to the general approval, Black-out Period and Inside Information rules.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure that limits the economic risk of holding the securities falls within the Derivatives(b) definition and so is banned outright over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: Over vested, unrestricted shares, a monetisation is at minimum an agreement to dispose of securities, which is a Deal requiring prior written approval, and would separately need to satisfy the Derivatives(b) risk-limiting-product rule if structured with a floor/cap.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of, securities

rules.detail: Outright ban, with no consent route stated.
rules.evidence: Employees must not engage in short selling of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

A CFD is a derivative within the meaning of s761D of the Corporations Act (the defined term's non-exhaustive list already includes options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants and collars) and so is banned outright over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: A CFD over vested, unrestricted shares is treated as a Derivative permitted subject to the law and the rest of the Policy (approval, Black-out Periods, Inside Information).
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on entering a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities; no security-state carve-out and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Employees may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement, i.e. any pledge/charge of the shares to secure borrowing; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: 'Margin Loan' is defined broadly as any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money using existing investments as security, and both entering such an arrangement and using Company Securities as its security are banned outright, catching any bank loan secured on the shares, not just broker margin loans.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, overriding anything else in the policy, on short term trading, illustrated by a 12-month purchase-with-intent-to-sell example.
rules.evidence: Despite anything to the contrary in this Policy, Employees must not engage in short term trading of any of Company Securities. An example of this would be to purchase the Company's shares with an intention to sell them within a 12 month period.

clearance.approver: Executive Director or the Chief Executive Officer
clearance.evidence: In the case of an Employee, prior written approval to Deal in Company Securities must be obtained from an Executive Director or the Chief Executive Officer.

clearance.approver: Chair (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee)
clearance.evidence: In the case of a Director, prior written approval to Deal in Company Securities must be obtained from the Chair (or in the case of the Chair, from the Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee).

A consultant or contractor (who is not an Employee) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.

short_term.evidence: An example of this would be to purchase the Company's shares with an intention to sell them within a 12 month period.

exceptions.evidence: transfer Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Employee is a beneficiary

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a scheme of arrangement, rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board.

exercise (but not Deal with the securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period

acquire (but not Deal with the securities following acquisition) Company shares by conversion of financial instruments giving rights to conversion to shares (eg. options or convertible securities) where the final date for the conversion of the security falls during a Black-out Period
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class

acquire, or agree to acquire, Company securities under an employee securities plan, including acquiring ordinary shares or other securities in the Company as a result of the vesting (including as a result of meeting performance hurdles, or by way of the release of Company securities from holding lock or the expiry of a holding term) or exercise of options or rights granted under such a plan
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Employee in an employee share plan where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan

where the Employee is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Employee.

exceptions.approver: Chair (Approval Officer), or Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair; or the Board
exceptions.evidence: the Employee is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities

exceptions.approver: Chair (Approval Officer), or Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair; or the Board
exceptions.evidence: the Employee is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement for them to do so

exemption_authority: The Approval Officer (Chair, or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair's own dealings) or the Board may grant written Disposal Consent to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period, only in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court order/legal requirement), only if the Employee is not in possession of Inside Information, and on terms and conditions considered reasonable, including the duration of the right to dispose or transfer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Combined with the outright ban on using Company Securities as security for 'a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement' (6.3(b)), this generic definition extends beyond broker margin loans to catch any bank loan secured against the collared shares, so the funded leg of a collar is banned outright with no clearance path.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly contemplates 'collars' as a derivative instrument, confirming a purchased put/written call structure is squarely within scope of the derivatives/hedging restrictions rather than an interpretive stretch.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an Employee may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the hardship/court-order exception route only ever permits a sale or transfer during a Black-out Period, not entry into a new derivative or financing arrangement, so a collar cannot be established, and its loan cannot be secured, under this exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A consultant or contractor (who is not an Employee) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This narrow, unlikely-to-apply tier escapes the Black-out Period, approval and margin loan restrictions altogether, but a director or senior executive holding vested equity would not typically qualify.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy. The derivative legs (a purchased put and written call are expressly contemplated as 'collars' within the Derivatives definition) are banned outright over unvested equity instruments and vested shares subject to a Holding Lock or other disposal restriction, with no consent route; once shares are vested and unrestricted, derivatives may be used only with prior written approval (Executive Director/CEO, or the Chair for Directors), outside the 15-trading-day pre-results/24-hour post-results Black-out Periods and any ad hoc black-out, and absent Inside Information. The loan leg is fatal regardless of vesting state: section 6.3 bans both borrowing to acquire Company Securities and using Company Securities as security for 'a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement', a term broadly defined to cover any lending arrangement secured by existing investments, with no clearance or hardship exception available - the only hardship/court-order exception permits disposal or transfer, not encumbrance or new financing. Consultants and contractors who are not 'Employees' escape the Black-out Period, approval and margin loan restrictions, but this narrow population is unlikely to include a director or senior executive holding vested equity for a collar. Overall, the derivative legs might clear on vested, unrestricted shares with prior approval, but the secured loan is expressly and absolutely prohibited, so a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented.
